name: Badger Maps
description: Badger Maps is a field-sales mapping and route-planning platform for visualizing customer and prospect records, optimizing multi-stop routes, managing territories, recording location-aware activity, and synchronizing field updates with CRM systems.
agentUseSummary: Badger Maps includes customer API/developer-key access and documents a Badger-owned Zapier integration, but its public material does not publish the external API base URL, endpoint and schema reference, authentication format, revocation behavior, webhook contract, or third-party application and distribution terms required for a bounded Relay connector. Relay therefore does not capture Badger API keys, imitate Zapier, automate product surfaces, or expose agent actions.

providerSetup.blocker: Badger Maps advertises customer API/developer-key access and a 25,000-request daily team limit, and it documents enabling and copying that key for its Zapier integration. Public official material does not provide an external API base URL, endpoint and schema reference, direct authentication format, revocation contract, webhooks, or third-party application and distribution terms. Its CRM integrations are described as Badger-built, Zapier-mediated, support-assisted, or custom deployments rather than a public developer platform.
providerSetup.nextAction: Reassess only if Badger Maps publishes a stable external third-party API with explicit authentication, permissions, endpoints, schemas, distribution terms, revocation, webhooks where applicable, and bounded non-communication reads suitable for Relay.

evidence.supports: Official pricing identifies Badger Maps as a field-sales mapping, route-optimization, territory-management, lead-generation, activity-reporting, and CRM-synchronization product. It includes customer API/developer-key access with a 25,000-request daily team limit, but publishes no endpoint or schema contract.

The official Zapier guide requires customers to ask support to turn on their API key, copy that key from Badger settings into Zapier, and use provider-defined account, check-in, user, photo, and route operations; it does not document direct HTTP endpoints, schemas, authentication headers, revocation, or external application registration.

Official CRM integration guidance offers Badger-built bidirectional connectors, Zapier, support-assisted FTP deployment, CSV import, and CRM links. It directs customized integrations through Badger staff rather than publishing a third-party developer contract.

Official terms make API-key access a limited, non-transferable, revocable customer license capped at 25,000 requests per day per team, require customer security controls, and prohibit bulk data access, third-party-benefit use, reverse engineering, and access through unprovided technology.

Official security material describes AWS hosting, TLS in transit, encrypted backups, SSO and SCIM, HIPAA, GDPR, and 42 CFR Part 2 controls for customer data, supporting critical handling of the provider's location and customer records.

Official privacy material covers contact, account, company, billing, calendar, camera, device, geographic-position, precise-location, payment, interaction, and user-provided data, reinforcing the decision not to capture credentials or automate private surfaces without a bounded supported contract.
